description.narrative: Project Outcomes Stakeholders. Environmental effect. The Project will reduce the carbon footprint of Element Fleet's clients by increasing the available fleet of electric vehicles for lease or purchase. The Project will support the Company's purchase of medium size trucks, minivans, and light commercial vehicles as well as compatible charging infrastructure. The proposed investment will contribute to Mexico's commitment to the Paris Agreement of reaching a 35 percent reduction in CO2 emissions below 2007 levels by the year 2030, particularly where commercial vehicles, given their greater number of daily kilometers travelled, present a larger opportunity for carbon reduction than personal vehicles. Overall, the transport sector is currently responsible for nearly 25-30% of Mexico's emissions and road transport represents more than 80 percent of the sector's emissions. Market Level Sustainability/Competitiveness: Elements services provided with EV fleets enable users to benefit from a more cost-effective asset-light operation in an environmentally sustainable manner. The Project is expected to demonstrate the viability of the EV-based fleet service model, inducing a wider adoption among commercial/business users and ultimately reducing their carbon footprint and contributing to the decarbonization of the transport sector. Greater adoption of EVs among Element clients would be demonstrated through a higher proportion of EVs among Elements vehicles under management (VUM) metric, which shows the number of vehicles that are being managed by Element and its subsidiaries.

The proposed investment entails a local currency-denominated (Mexican Pesos) senior loan of up to US$100 million equivalent in MXN to Element Fleet Management Corporation (Element or the Company) and its Mexican subsidiariesElement Fleet Management Corporation México, S.A. de C.V., and Element Fleet México, S.A. de C.V., SOFOM, E.N.R. (Element Mexico Subsidiaries) for the acquisition of EVs (passenger cars, last-mile trucks, and vans) and investment in associated charging infrastructure (the Project).
